Dr. Selleri is the most suitable instructor in ELIT if you wish to fully immerse yourself in the course material. He is engaging, energetic, accommodating, and helpful (when he's not rushing through lectures because he overestimated how many texts we could fit in two hours, that is). I never had a question go unanswered, and every contribution from each student was met with a welcoming response. I do wish he had been a little easier on the workload this semester, considering the earthquake and the state of the students in its aftermath.

instructor: Andrea is great. He knows what he's talking about. His dry humor is a welcome bonus.

Dr. Selleri demanded my (our) full attention in exchange for what is by far the most informative course I have ever taken on this campus (and I've been department-hopping here for five years now, so you can put some gravity on that statement). I gave him my time and energy, he gave me his time and energy three or four times back.

It is unfathomable to me that anyone would describe him as unapproachable. I have barged into his office many times just to chat (almost exclusively about philosophers he loathes, mind you) and he has never not taken me seriously, has never made me feel like I was in any way his inferior, has never been anything less than friendly and charitable, and has given me a baffling amount to read and to look into.

Quick round: he has absolutely killer taste in music, his sense of humor is phenomenal, despite his hesitation to call himself a philosopher he is a more competent philosophy lecturer than almost the entirety of the school's philosophy department, he carries himself so well and speaks so eloquently that I would happily listen to a two-hour lecture by him given fully in Italian or French despite not understanding a single word, and he allows for (if not directly encourages) almost absurd levels of creative freedom for his assignments. I also feel the need to note that he has graded my work very generously, and I am by no means an extraordinary student, so I'm not sure how his reputation as a lousy grader came to be.

If he hates teaching he's doing a terrific job at hiding it, considering the amount of time he's willing to dedicate to each student and how much he visibly cares for and dotes on the material he teaches. I have seen and received nothing but completely reasonable academic rigor, stunning intellectual vigor, honest feedback, sincere encouragement, and an astonishing amount of knowledge from him.

If this reads as overly fawning it's because anything less would be gross dishonesty on my part. I can't thank him enough.
course: Probably the best course in the department

This course was the first time I was ever asked to read and analyze Hegel in any capacity throughout my undergraduate education, which is in political science. Considering that I have taken every theory-focused political science course I could have, this is a gorgeous triumph on Dr. Selleri's end and a revolting failure on my department's.

I think the course is characterized by triumphs of this exact kind: the syllabus is absolutely jam-packed yet not a single reading feels even slightly out of place, so you find yourself constantly amazed that a lot of it is material you've never read before, and the way those bleed into and connect with the ones you have read (in my case a very limited amount of Kant, Kierkegaard, and Wilde) gives the kind of intense satisfaction that results in intense motivation to read more, learn more, draw more connections, bite and pull harder. I was not demotivated for a single second.

I will say that I would not recommend this course to anyone who has a habit of skipping lectures as some of the readings are rather dense, and Dr. Selleri does a fantastic job at making them easier to digest and tying the strings between them (into lovely ribbons). Again, this is a course that demands your full attention and rewards you generously for it.

I think this course does a great job of incorporating readings from the philosophy of art and art criticism into a literature class. We've engaged with more "big picture" stuff, which I found extremely useful and educational. We should have more courses like this along with our regular literature classes.

His classes were generally extremely boring. I had a hard time paying attention in most of his classes. Even though some topics were interesting, the way he taught them was not. I made a great effort to keep my eyes open and not fall asleep. Except for a few people participating in the class, the rest of the class remained silent. course: Oral examinations, whether midterms or finals, increase my anxiety levels. I would prefer if they were structured as either take-home exams or in-class written assessments.

This course was one of the ones I learnt most from. Although most courses' content and operation is usually based on the instructor, this course itself was one that helps engage with close reading texts and analyse different literature in different ways. So, great course, although quite difficult if you don't put in the work.
The course has a heavier workload compared to other ELIT courses but since the things covered in this course are necessary for everyone in this department, it is okay.
Ders keyifli geçti benim için. Bir edebiyat öğrencisi için olmazsa olmaz şiir hakkında pek çok şey öğrendim.

I think I learned the maximum I could in one course because it has a very rich content. A great lesson for those who study and love the lesson.

I think attendance is a bit of an issue. As students we have a couple hours of absences given to us and I believe we should be able to use those without having to deal with their effect on our participation points.

instructor: Her şeyi bilen kişi kendisi ve siz hiçbir şey bilmiyormuşsunuz gibi davranıyor, öğrencilere çok yukardan bakıyor. Not konusunda zaten çok katı. Kasıntı birisi

He is very knowledgeable and truly knows what he is doing. I really admire him in this regard. It is true that his grades are not very high, especially the participation grade, which shocked me. Apart from that, I believe that if you attend the classes, you can learn a lot from him.

notlandırması özellikle participationda iğrenç ötesi. Ne kadar çok forum a yazarsanız yazın ya da ne kadar derse katılırsanız katılın 100 diye bir şey yok. ayrıca derse gelmediğiniz zaman durum ne olursa olsun puanınızı etkiliyor...   70'in D ye tekabül etmesi kadar da saçma bir şey olamaz.

Dr. Selleri is helpful and tries his best to learn and discover your interests. I have learned a lot about different topics with the help of his guidance. He answered many questions I asked, guiding me to read even more and comprehend better. I have learned about poetics, linguistics, critical theory, cognitive poetics, and philosophy. He is always passionate about teaching and learning new things, which inspires me. I believe that his interdisciplinary perspective helps students to widen their understanding of literature. Bazı konularda hocamızın iletişime cok açık olmadığını düşünüyorum ancak işini fazlasıyla iyi bilen alanında tutkulu ve fikrimce başarılı bir hoca

To me, it felt like he didn't have a strict grading criteria and graded students in a somewhat instinctual way. The abstract syllabus guidelines didn't help much either. So, there might be some instances, for example, where you participate more in class but get less participation grades due to this ambigious grading system.

While teaching, he looks like he doesnt enjoy being in the classroom. His lectures are REALLY boring and hard to be focused on after some time. It is obvious he is very knowledgeable and loves literature, but I cant say the same thing about him being a teacher. I looked forward for his lectures to end.

He is the most knowledgeable instructor in this country who teaches the art of poetry. I'm pretty sure that this course will bring about the worst GPA you will ever get in Bilkent, but also  the one you will learn the most.

unstressed stressed kavramlarını anlayabilmek için 15 tane video izledim... türk bir öğrenci olarak vurgu anlamak bence zor.

I think we go through some poems too quickly. Instead, the number of poems could be reduced, and spend more time diving into each one in detail.

Finalin sözlü şeklinde yapılmasını mantıklı bulmuyorum fikrince öğrencinin performansını düşüren ve genel anlamda anksiyeteye sebebiyet veren bir yöntem

instructor: he is scary and funny, i don't know if i like him or not

Dr Selleri is obviously very knowledgeable about this topic but it's really hard to catch up with him in class. He also makes it hard to participate in class and grades poorly. gerçekten korkunç birisi.

bölümdeki en bilgili hoca olabilir, sadece huyuna gidebilmeniz önemli; bir şeyler öğrendiğinizi veya efor sarf ettiğinizi görmek istiyor. yoksa düşük alabilirsiniz :) bir de sarcastic bir insandır kendisi, fazla alınmayın.

Despite some of the reviews I've seen, he was actually quite enthusiastic about what he taught. If you care enough about the course, you are sure to get something from it. His teaching was efficient and concise, and his (dry) humour made the classes very enjoyable

course: It was an interesting course overall. I think taking this course from Dr. Selleri is a good idea with his dramatization of each poems' spirit.

the syllabus is way too loaded. there were wayyy too many things that we were responsible to know about. the tasks were really hard. we analyzed 5 poems plus one aspect of poetry each week and we had to know all of these for the final exam.
assistant: I think he should be warned about building simple conversations with his students.

instructor: "mad, bad, and dangerous to know."
course:
I enjoyed it! We probably would have benefited from having guiding questions assigned with the readings (rather than trying to come up with answers on the spot, as it led to some awkward silences every now and then). The discussion leadings also became an issue with the small class size. I liked the seminar-based structure, though: it made for creative & engaging discussions, which is not something you get with lecture-heavy classes. The readings were interesting, the assignments manageable, and the class overall great. Dr. Selleri is often the instructor from whom I learn the most, so I appreciated being able to revisit a poetry class and leave it knowing a great deal more about poems of ideas than before. 

The worst part was the number of 8:30 classes, which I'm sure is against the Geneva Convention in some way.

instructor: I think for the participation, the instructor should be more courageous toward the students

There's no doubt Mr. Andrea knows what he teaches, and I think he can convey them very well. The texts he chose are -mostly- fun to read, and I liked how he structured the syllabus around themes. The real issue with this class is its participation policy and how Mr. Andrea evaluates assignments. I'm not sure what one has to do to get high participation grades. Whereas other teachers simply expect a student to talk when they feel like it, and grade participation on a basis of understanding, Mr. Andrea's grading is simply brutal. It is literally impossible to get a good grade (and no, I'm not the only one. Many people I've talked to complain about this as well). While he might think he's being objective, it conveys like he's trying hard to make this class a burden. I get that it's a teacher's right to expect in-class participation, but I think he simply expects too much. This wouldn't be a problem if he was using a kind of curve system for letter grades, but no. It is according to the grading table (which, to be honest, is also brutal) so you know you will get a low grade. I like him as a teacher but I just wish he didn't grade things. Another thing is his use of spare hours. He uses the spare hours almost every week, which is also unnecessary. I feel like we could still learn a lot from him without waking up at 6 every monday.

The only thing I can say is Gloria Gaynor made the song  "I Will Survive" with this course given by this instructor in mind. Not getting an FZ and additionally passing the course could cause having a god complex since you are probably going to be one of the few that was able to do so.
course: If I had the chance to absolutely exterminate a course, it would be this one.

instructor: He seemed like he is not happy to be here to teach throughout the semester. He did not even looked to the class at all. He was mostly just talking to himself about the opinions of some philosophers and some examples from literature.

Andrea hoca üniversite hayatımda bana en düşük notları veren hocaydı. Dersleri aşırı sıkıcı. Sesini tek bir tonda tutuyor ve öğrenciyi asla derse kanalize edemiyor. Bu yüzden dersine kimse gelmiyor. Ayrıca aşırı kaba bir insan, koridorda görünce göz teması bile kurmaktan kaçıyor.
He has an incredible knowledge. It was great to be a listener and a student of him. Thank you Andrea,
Never getting a high grade no matter how much you try was the best part of this class.

Even though I thought that it will be beneficial to take this course, there were many moments when I felt like I regretted it. Even if you think you put in a good performance, that's not enough for him but dont worry,  If you can withstand the hurtful comments, the course will be very easy.

He welcomes everyone's contributions, even if the contributions are out of the box answers.

He has a lot of knowledge but expects us to have that kind of knowledge, and when we do not, he gets disappointed and shows it clearly. He is also a perfectionist; it is hard to find him liking a thing you say or write.
course:

filled to the brim

instructor: The instructor is knowledgeable, yes, but the course is marked by an exceptionally high workload and demanding requirements. This poses the risk of student stress, burnout, and a potentially counterproductive learning environment. The grading is too harsh. The instructor will say that he likes an essay but still gives a low grade.  There are too many demands on participation too. No other class I've taken has this much weight on participation. It is very hard to follow when the assignments are due. I was confused with the excesssive amount of reading material, which is hard to keep up with since other courses' instructors want us to read other works too.

He swallows the words, it is hard to understand what he is talking about. When someone is presenting I find myself understanding the material better. 

Takes himself way too seriously and disrespects students outside class.
cant teach novels. he should stick to poetry.

The workload is heavy and the grading is way too harsh for the time and effort we put in these assignments. The oral aspects of the course are too demanding and even unrealistic, I think the students might have spoken as much as the instructor did, perhaps even more. The instructor is definitely competent in the course material but is not effectively imparting this knowledge to the students. We knew this course would be demanding but that does not mean it is always in the right to be so, especially if the students end up disliking the course due to its unrealistic demands.

This is the second time I took a class from him, and I am positive that he is quite sophisticated and highly intellectual, and I still have lots to learn from him. The source material and the coursepack overall consisted of intriguing texts and he gave us the opportunity to be practically free to choose how our midterm would ensue. I think that asides from the fact that he’s a bit of a perfectionist, he completely gets you in the soul of academia. If you understand what he wants and expects from the students, you can learn a lot from him and have a good experience throroughly.

Dr. Selleri was stimulating in class, making us ask questions and lead some of the discussion ourselves. The freedom he provided us with was helpful, and his communication and expectations were clear.

Dr. Selleri is still Dr. Selleri. He picks interesting texts, incentivizes intellectually stimulating discussions, and then manages to rush through those texts in a way that leaves no space for those discussions to take place. The greatest thing about taking a class from him is his willingness to communicate: his feedback on assignments is constructive and detailed, and he is always willing to answer any questions one might have about the course content. His humorous teaching style makes the lectures notably engaging. His biggest problem, though, is time management: we barely get to discuss the texts beyond the first page, and when we do, it feels like we're being chased by an army of feral horses.
course:
The course is interesting and offers many point of views for many different material.

It also insists upon itself and starts to see any kind of emotion or emotional outburst as madness or mental illness.

Assuming that this is a literature course, the main aspects of the course should be reading, analyzing and writing. Almost 70% of the course relies on the discussion/presentation/oral examination of the student. I am not sure how such emphasis on oral expression contributes to strengthening one's knowledge and understanding of literature. I chose this degree because I wanted to write and express my ideas on paper, just like the writers and poets we study in class. If I wanted to express my ideas orally all the time, I would have chosen a different path. The course is very promising, but fails to develop our sense of "madness in literature" on paper, and rather makes us teach the topics we should instead be taught. I am also not sure how memorizing and being tested on the details of the works we have studied at the very beginning of the class will be of any merit? Again, this all boils down to the teaching and evaluation styles of the course, which in my opinion, lacks the understanding of what a literature student should be doing.

It feels like the first and second halves of ELIT 426 were completely different classes. We began with a lot of energy, but as we moved further into the semester, all sense of engagement disappeared. The readings were already too much, but in combination with people's presentations (twenty minutes each), it became impossible to talk about anything in a meaningful way. There was little space for insightful conversation. This would have been my favourite class of the term if we had not sped through it. However, I did appreciate the final oral exam, as well as the Moodle forums available for student participation.
The course, albeit packed, was fun to get through and there was not one text I disliked reading and discussing in class.
feedbackleri bazen gereksiz ve anlamsizdi (“?”)

strong points: the readings were interesting and had a lot of variety. i liked that we had secondary readings because they helped with understanding the main texts. the mad woman in the attic was one of my favourites, especially since it wasnt a text id expect to see in dr selleri's class. 
weak points: the reading load was heavy, but the problem was that the course didn't have enough hours for us to actually have any discussions about the readings. wuthering Heights was a nightmare. the discussions surrounding it only had to do with how much everyone was in love with heathcliff.
This was one of the most difficult courses i've ever taken

instructor: Dr. Selleri is clearly an expert in his field and it is obvious that he loves his expertise. But, I don't really think that he is successful in teaching as he is in reading and analyzing. At the beginning of semester, he said that he understands that everyone has a different schedule and he said that he wants to choose the date for the midterms and finals accordingly so that the majority - 3rd year students - do not affect in a bad way. It was thoughtful and this sentence made me feel optimistic and excited about the class. However, the classes were unbearable, he made some weird jokes in class, in his feedbacks, in the private meetings in his office; he missed so many morning classes since he fell asleep and took a sleeping pill as he confessed, he did not even look to the class, he just talked with himself. He always seemed unhappy being in class and in Turkey in general as he made abundantly clear multiple times with his unfunny jokes. He gives such a negative vibe that you do not really feel like going to class.
Super sweet, super interested in the material, makes sure to pick interesting reading material in class and engages well with them.

He is a really qualified instructor. I like his long and educational answers to the moodle forums; they are detailed and add more to my understanding of the topic. I also appreciate the summary notes he puts under every article, they help me a lot.

But I think he should have given us prompts for the final because the lecture was already hard to understand and it gave me stress to find a thesis.

He has great knowledge of literature in general and he always gives us different types of texts and writers in the course which lead to diversity and it is helpful. Whenever you ask something about anything you do not understand or whenever you present your thoughts, he adds more information and advises books or any other sources that will help you. He never ignores his students and he helps as much as possible. Also, his feedbacks are so helpful and detailed which is important for our department. Though at first, it seems harsh, you know that it is for your own good to improve yourself. He is fair in grading. And I appreciate how he remembers everything like even line and page numbers, he has a great memory which is quite impressive.

Being knowledgeable does not make one a good teacher, therefore, he needs to work on how to teach things rather than showing off his knowledge.
During the courses, he never took attendance but in the syllabus, there is a section on attendance and participation grading.
He came to class late three times, for some students, it takes a lot of time to come to campus for the morning classes.
He needs to learn how to interact with the students, most of the time he just talks by himself as if we were listening to a pre-recorded voice recording. 
 Not approachable, considering ELIT department professors, he is the most distant one. 
Literary theory is a boring class, he made it worse. He is very sophisticated but his teaching style does not charm me, to be honest.
course: it is complicated sometimes because of the authors' use of language, and we make a lot of reading through the semester and it is hard to catch up (especially when we have other classes' readings). Literary theory is not my interest, I simply just like enjoying my reading.
The required books were so expensive for everyone to buy.
Literary Theory is boring and needs to be revised. Rather than reading lots of things, there should be a mechanism to make it more approachable.

The course is generally more overwhelming than the other courses we take because there are lots of theories and terms that we need to memorize. And some theories are complicated. But the course also helps us to learn the frame of the literature and analyze texts much better.

instructor: Mr. Selleri was able to make the course interesting despite it being completely theoretical. Overall, I really enjoyed his teaching!
A knowledgeable and a quite smart instructor

I feel so unlucky that I had no other choice than Andrea Selleri to take this course. I wish there could be another teacher giving this course because it would be more fun and fair. He did not give me the grades that I deserved, I hope I will not have any other course that I must take from him.
course: I think the course would be more intriguing if there had been more focus on the interpretation of literary works based on what was taught at class. Lastly, it would be better to give a reading assignment from Possession each week for it would ensure the continuity of the reading of it. Still, the course was fun!
The course could have been beneficial if the instructor had not been Andrea Selleri.
Very interesting course material, can be boring to get through sometimes

instructor: Dr. Selleri is funny however that is not enough for an instructor. He does not know what he wants from the students therefore gives interesting grades.

As one of the rare students who used to like Dr. Selleri’s classes a lot, the kindest thing I can say is that this semester was not ideal. Overall, this semester was a bit complicated due to the unpleasant events that happened. Although he was not the only one who was affected by those events and their consequences (students and other instructors have been affected by the same events), he acted like all those changes only affected him. I never said that the students were the angels, who were eager to learn, but he didn’t even seem like he was interested in what he was teaching. The way he teaches is by projecting an article to the board and then reading the lines he has highlighted before. When we did the same thing on debate days, we got a C because we didn’t do anything but summarize, which is a bit ironic. Also, there wasn’t even a clear guide on what he expected from debate days (no one even knew what their topic was to the point where two of the groups supported the same side because they didn’t understand which side they had been put on). He definitely enjoys giving low grades (it is a fact that everyone knows in this department), but this is not the problem. The real problem is that he started being rude while giving feedback. His feedback became his way of taking revenge because he hadn’t been appreciated as much as he expected, and we couldn’t keep up with his unrealistic expectations.

Although he started the semester with great energy, as we progressed through the semester his professionalism started to decrease. Of course, this semester was not an easy one but instead of making the class more bearable, he made sure that we were suffering even more. He always portrayed a lack of interest in his lectures. Grading and feedbacks are another story. I have taken other courses from him and I always told my peers about his fair and informative feedback, but this course has been a nightmare both grading and feedback-wise. His feedback became less about helping us to improve and more of a tool for him to drag us down.

I think he reflected his personal problems in his teaching, I never saw him happy in class, he was in a constant state of anxiety. And I think he was unfair in his marking, even if we did successful research on the subject we were studying, he found faults and mistakes with it. This demotivates the student.
No weak points. He is passionate about the lecture he gives which is excellent.
course: Due to the lack of interest of the instructor, the lectures were more like reading a text from the computer and saying a few words about it. There was one engaging activity for this whole semester.
This course had the potential to be very important and improving but it was just a disappointment.
No weak points. It enables one to think in a philosophical and critical way about literature as a phenomenon.

I cannot see a positive side to it, I think students do not get efficiency from this course because of the way the course is taught, although it could be one of the most useful courses in this department.
The material for the course were fun however debate was unnecessary. Individual session concept is great.

instructor:
I will start by saying this: Professor Selleri clearly knows so much. I respect his knowledge of many things and his opinions, and I think he is very interested in his teachings. Although I got okay-ish grades, I never complained much because he justified his grading well, and I always learned something from it. However, he seems not to like his students or his job. This year, he complained a lot about the earthquake and how our school handled it (which, I agree, was very confusing for teachers and students). But I believe he took his dissatisfaction from us. Personally, I was not affected by the earthquake; however, the school's on-and-off decisions did not ONLY affect him, but it also affected us too, and he seemed to disregard that. He was a little too passive-aggressive, and I think for this course, he treated us like we were master's degree students. Again, I envy and even understand his seriousness and passion for English Literature as well as what he does for his course, but in my opinion, he could have been more "chill." 
In the end, I think you can learn A LOT from him. He is just different from what we are used to.

Mr. Selleri seemed to hate the department, the course and the students. Often times he was visibly bored and frustrated. It was not fun to read many mails long bouts of frustrations, mostly directed toward himself or the school. 

He used a system of grading participation that made no sense. I got few points for the week that I did not attend classes in-person at all, meanwhile I got 0 in a week where I actively attended classes and participated in the class discussion. After the presentation part of one debate day, Mr. Selleri only allowed for 8 minutes of actual debate, afterward, claiming he had places to go and things to do, promised he would open up a Moodle forum so that like other groups, this group too could debate. That Moodle forum never came to be, he said it would be unfair to other groups. The other groups had more time to discuss, the 8 minute debate group didn't.

Mr. Selleri's feedback for the assignments included many snide remarks and passive-aggressive comments. And I know this was not special treatment for my feedbacks personally, as he shared another student's feedback with the whole class through mail by accident, which was as snarky as mine. His language and attitude in writing made it very difficult to make use of the feedback, I felt like I was constantly being berated while trying to get some use out of the feedbacks for the final essay. 

I know he doesn't hate me, but his actions and words through the semester sure made me feel like he did.
I know I will be identified by what I have written, but I don't care. Nobody, even a "bad" student like me, deserves to be treated like how he treated me and other students in the class.
He should reevaluate his acts that make him seem like “students always think and act the worst, even in situations where disasters leave them traumatized” because the way he tried to get ahead on any “slacking” was rude and unkind.
He is a valuable figure in the ELIT department. But too much concentrated on aesthetics. He is highly intellectual, a little bit perfectionist and expects too much from the students.
The strongest point is that he is very knowledgeable, and the weakest is that he is very strict.

Dr Selleri is very knowledgeable, but I don't think he has enough patience and love for students to be an instructor. His grading system is rigid for most of us, I think he sometimes forgets the fact that we are trying to get our bachelor's degrees, we are not here for master's. We are all aware that this lesson is more difficult than the others since it is a theoretical one, but Dr Selleri's attitude towards us makes it harder to concentrate. Since the beginning of the semester, I was always very stressed every time I thought about this lesson. Especially in this period when everything was difficult, he did not show understanding to his students.

Positive aspects: Promoting students to apply theories into practice much and also encourages us to make comprehensive and intellectual research.
Negative aspects: Most of the readings that we covered in class are complex to comprehend  and extract a meaning to apply into theories in one class, so does the contribute to participation. Additionally, ı'd expect him to be more flexible while grading participations since it was the hardest semester to follow and attend lectures due to the earthquake related problems and regulations, and also two elections  that required students to travel.

The issue with Prof. Selleri is that he is highly overqualified for the job. He is sophisticated and wise, yet from just one class, you can clearly see that he does not like teaching. He is a strict perfectionist. I Would not recommend his classes. Andrea will immediately know if you are not ready to do your best and give your best effort for his task. An underrated quality of his is that he is a pretty sarcastic guy who tries his best to be fun in the class setting. He is way more understanding and calm during the face-to-face examinations.
course: The strongest is that the course covers a lot of different kinds of material and the weakest is that it is expecting a lot, like we do not have other courses.
